rektion: jdn./etw. (Akk.) durchschauen (einen Trick, eine Lüge, einen Plan, jdn. durchschauen)
meaning_en: to see through (someone, a trick, a lie)
definition_de: erkennen, was jemand wirklich vorhat oder dass etwas nicht stimmt (Ich habe dich durchschaut!). Trennbar (dúrchschauen, hat durchgeschaut) heißt es 'etwas Stück für Stück ansehen und prüfen'.
example_de: Die Mutter durchschaut die Ausrede ihres Sohnes sofort, denn er hat noch Schokolade im Gesicht.
example_en: The mother sees through her son's excuse immediately, because he still has chocolate on his face.
visual_idea: Collocation 'eine Ausrede / jdn. durchschauen': a boy with an innocent face and chocolate smeared around his mouth, an empty chocolate wrapper behind his back, and his mother with crossed arms and a knowing smile. The visible proof makes 'she sees through it' instantly clear, and it is funny. Rejected: a poker bluff (cards attract symbols and text) and a phone scam (a screen with text).
image_prompt: a bright German family kitchen, a six-year-old boy stands with a wide innocent smile and big eyes, his mouth and cheeks clearly smeared with brown chocolate, both hands hidden behind his back holding a crumpled plain brown wrapper that the viewer can see, his mother stands in front of him with crossed arms, one eyebrow raised and a knowing smile, medium shot
negative_prompt: text, letters, watermark, signature, caption, blurry, extra fingers, deformed hands, cluttered background, multiple panels
video_prompt: a boy with chocolate on his face smiles innocently at his mother and shakes his head; she raises one eyebrow, points at his chocolate-smeared mouth and smiles knowingly, and he hides his face in his hands, caught; static medium shot
